ig_carousel_topic.topic: Bankroll math for people who've never thought about bankroll
ig_carousel_topic.slide1_text:
Most bettors lose not because they pick wrong.
They lose because they size wrong.
ig_carousel_topic.slide2_text:
The common approach: bet whatever feels right on whatever game feels good.
A big loss hits. You chase. The account bleeds out fast.
Feeling-based sizing is how bankrolls die.
ig_carousel_topic.slide3_text:
Flat betting fixes this. Pick a unit size, 1 to 2 percent of your total bankroll, and bet that amount on every single play.
A cold streak hurts less. A hot streak compounds cleanly.
ig_carousel_topic.slide4_text:
Example: $500 bankroll. One unit = $5 (1%).
You go 54-46 over 100 bets at -110 juice.
Net result: roughly +$38, or +7.6 units.
Same record with random sizing? You probably lost money.
ig_carousel_topic.slide5_text:
54 percent wins at flat 1% units builds a real edge over time.
The math only works if the sizing is consistent. Start there.
